title: Choking
summary: Recognize choking fast and use the right first-aid steps for adults, children, and infants.

sections.heading: Step 1 — Recognize choking
sections.body: A choking person may be unable to speak, cough effectively, or breathe. They may grab their throat, make high-pitched sounds, or go silent. If the person can cough forcefully, encourage coughing and stay ready to act if the airway becomes fully blocked.
sections.image_description: A person holding their throat with a universal choking sign.

sections.heading: Step 2 — Help an adult or child over one year
sections.body: Stand behind the person and lean them forward slightly. Give firm back blows between the shoulder blades, then abdominal thrusts if the object does not come out, following local first-aid guidance. Repeat the cycle until the airway clears or the person becomes unresponsive.
sections.warning: Do not perform abdominal thrusts on infants or on someone who is pregnant unless local emergency guidance specifically instructs chest thrusts.
sections.image_description: A rescuer delivering back blows to a leaning-forward adult.

sections.heading: Step 3 — Treat infant choking differently
sections.body: Infants under one year should be supported face-down along the forearm with the head lower than the chest. Give gentle back blows between the shoulder blades and chest thrusts if needed, not abdominal thrusts. Use only enough force to dislodge the object without injuring the infant.
sections.image_description: An infant supported face-down on a responder's forearm with back blows.

sections.heading: Step 4 — Call for emergency help
sections.body: Call emergency services immediately if the person cannot breathe, becomes blue, collapses, or loses consciousness. If they become unresponsive, start CPR if you are trained and follow dispatcher instructions. Even after the object comes out, the person may need medical care because swelling or injury can remain.
sections.warning: If you cannot get help quickly, continue first aid while another person calls emergency services.
sections.image_description: A phone with an emergency call icon next to a person receiving first aid.

when_to_use: Use this guide when food or another object is blocking the airway and the person is struggling to breathe or speak.
do_not: Do not do blind finger sweeps.
Do not delay emergency help if breathing stops.
